rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should explore a promising multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with scgpt (RNA) and imagenet_vit_l (image) encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion—components that are likely to capture complex interactions. It clarifies the potential effectiveness of combining strong encoders with advanced aggregation/fusion methods, which are critical for multimodal cellular profiling.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.52 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing the fusion method from 'weighted' to 'concat' while keeping other parameters identical. This clarifies whether the fusion strategy significantly impacts performance, allowing exploitation of the current promising multimodal setup. It's a low-risk, high-impact test of a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.519957). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other components the same, clarifying whether the image encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on the current best setup) and exploration (testing a key design choice with potential impact).

Existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests changing the image encoder to resnet50 and fusion to concat while keeping scgpt RNA and transformer aggregation, which are key components of the current top performer. It clarifies whether the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) and fusion method (concat vs weighted) significantly impact performance, balancing exploration of critical design choices with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that using scgpt RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_001) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation while retaining weighted fusion (config_038) could improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods, a critical design choice, without deviating from the top-performing RNA/image encoder pair. This balances exploitation of current strengths with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (config_038, 0.542 accuracy) is the strongest so far. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with the same avgpool and weighted setup, clarifying if RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on successful aggregation/fusion) and exploration (testing a new encoder).

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_046) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping other components the same) could further improve performance. It clarifies the optimal aggregation method for this high-performing RNA/image encoder pair, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of architectural variations.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion (e.g., config_042, 0.724989) perform best. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) in config_042's successful setup, clarifying if image encoder choice impacts performance. With limited budget, this directly explores a key hyperparameter while building on strong prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows config_042 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. The uncertainty is whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same RNA/image encoders affects performance. Testing config_013 (same RNA/image encoders and transformer aggregation but concat fusion) clarifies if fusion method is critical, balancing exploitation of current top performer with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_042, 049) achieve high accuracy (up to 0.725). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, which could improve performance by leveraging a different RNA feature extraction method while maintaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. It clarifies whether pca_n2000 offers better performance than scvi_n200 in this setup, directly addressing a key design choice with high potential impact.
